Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment consistent with acute infectious gastroenteritis: 3-day diarrhea with 4–5 loose/watery stools/day, mild abdominal pain, one vomiting episode, mild possible fever, no blood or mucus in stool, no travel or suspicious diet; patient appears not dehydrated and able to maintain fluid intake  
- Past asthma noted, inhaler use (“Lexapro”—unclear exact medication) unlikely causative but medication-induced diarrhea considered as medium likelihood differential diagnosis  
- Food intolerance (e.g., lactose intolerance) considered as moderate likelihood given prior episodes triggered by foods, but no current trigger identified, and acute onset less typical  
- Inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer considered less likely based on short duration, absence of blood or mucus, and young age, but family history of bowel cancer noted as relevant background information  
- No contradictions between transcript and DDx identified  

Management Plan
- Supportive management advised: maintain adequate hydration, adopt soft diet (crackers, toast, jam, mashed vegetables), avoid dairy, meat, fish, and eggs until diarrhea resolves for at least 48 hours before reintroducing these foods  
- Probiotic yogurts encouraged to help restore gut flora  
- Monitor for worsening symptoms: if diarrhea worsens (more than 6–8 times/day), blood appears in stool, or symptoms persist beyond one week, stool sample and further evaluation recommended  
- Oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) suggested to maintain electrolyte balance  
- Patient advised to seek further medical attention if signs of dehydration develop or symptoms worsen  
- All advice documented in app for patient review

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Acute infectious gastroenteritis: High likelihood; aligns closely with presentation of acute diarrhea, mild fever, vomiting, no blood/mucus, and duration (3 days)  
- Medication-induced diarrhea (possible inhaler side effect): Moderate likelihood; patient using inhaler “Lexapro,” unclear if causative; no medication changes  
- Food intolerance (e.g., lactose intolerance): Moderate likelihood; patient has history of food-related diarrhea but no current exposure or typical chronic course  
- Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD): Low likelihood; short duration, no blood/mucus, no chronic symptoms  
- Colorectal cancer: Low likelihood; noted family history but presentation and age not typical
